name: Moyogalpa
description: The main ferry port and largest town, with the most services on the island: the better of two ATMs, small grocery stores, pharmacies, scooter rental shops, and a strip of restaurants along the main street. It's the least scenic base but the most convenient for arrivals, errands, and onward travel.
pros: Most shops and services on the island
cons: Least scenic of the main towns

name: Balgue (Maderas side)
tagline: Jungle lodges under the crater volcano
description: A small village on the northeastern flank of Maderas volcano, surrounded by eco-lodges, permaculture farms, and yoga retreats. It's the closest base for hiking to the Maderas crater lake and San Ramon waterfall, with a loose backpacker and long-stay-traveler community forming around a handful of cafes.
bestFor: hikers, yoga and wellness travelers, longer slow stays
pros: Closest access to Maderas crater hike
cons: Rough unpaved roads in and out

name: Santa Cruz
tagline: Small crossroads town with lake views
description: A modest village between Moyogalpa and Balgue, known for lakeside views, a couple of traveler-friendly restaurants and hostels, and easy access to the isthmus beaches. It functions as a quieter, less touristy alternative to Balgue while still being close enough to Maderas-side attractions.
bestFor: budget travelers, those wanting a quieter middle-ground base
cons: Wifi and power even less reliable than main towns

name: Altagracia
tagline: The island's cultural and administrative heart
description: The second-largest town, on the Concepcion side, home to the island's other ATM, a small archaeology museum with pre-Columbian petroglyphs and statues, a lively central plaza, and the ferry connection to San Jorge. It has a more authentically Nicaraguan, less tourist-oriented feel than Moyogalpa.
bestFor: culture-focused travelers, those wanting authenticity over polish
cons: Limited English spoken outside a few spots
